verdict.rationale: Mailgun documents per-domain scoped credentials: Domain Sending Keys can only send for the domain they were created in. It also documents IP pool management for sender reputation, and a community user confirms running separate domains with dedicated IPs at scale. Per-tenant isolation of suppression lists and a subaccount model are not evidenced. Missing for 10: subaccount/subuser documentation, per-domain suppression list isolation, explicit per-tenant reputation separation docs, independent corroboration of tenant isolation.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can isolate tenants — subaccounts, subusers, or multiple domains with separate credentials, suppression lists, and reputation — for the platform I'm building

citations.quote: Domain Sending Keys are API keys that only allow sending messages via a POST call on /messages and /messages.mime endpoints for the domain in which they are created for.
Manage IP pools to optimize email delivery and maintain sender reputation.
Working flawlessly, given that you setup everything correctly (separate domains, dedicated IPs...).
